also: you’ve got it on back to front

terms.gloss: in reversed order, the wrong way round
evidence: Plin. NH 2.24: laevus calceus praeposterē inductus (Lewis & Short s.v. praeposterus)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “in a reversed order, irregularly”. Pliny has it of a shoe put on the wrong foot; of clothes put on back to front, praeposterē induere (our phrase).

evidence: Suet. Aug. 92: sī māne sibi calceus perperam ac sinister prō dextrō indūcerētur
terms.comment: Suetonius’s word for a shoe put on the wrong foot, the left for the right. Pliny tells the same of Augustus with praeposterē.

phrases.english: to put on back to front

phrases.latin: Calceōs praeposterē induistī; sinister est in dextrō pede.
phrases.english: You’ve put your shoes on the wrong feet; the left one is on your right foot.

phrases.latin: Dīvus Augustus prōdidit laevum sibi calceum praeposterē inductum quō diē sēditiōne mīlitārī prope adflīctus est.
phrases.english: The Deified Augustus recorded that on the day a mutiny of the soldiers nearly overthrew him he had put his left shoe on the wrong foot.

phrases.latin: sī māne sibi calceus perperam ac sinister prō dextrō indūcerētur, ut dīrum
phrases.english: if in the morning his shoe was put on wrongly, the left for the right, he took it as a bad omen

sources: Lewis & Short: praeposterus · Lewis & Short: perperam
